clue.text: Apparently wins support, though contradicted

parts.note: wins means gains, as in gains ground
support means aid or help

explanation.surface: Someone seemingly gaining backing is nonetheless opposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' tells you to read the answer as two words, GAINS AID, which is what winning support looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or speak against, so a statement gainsaid has been disputed.

clue.text: Refined chap with a slippery customer

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a chap
an eel is proverbially slippery

explanation.surface: A cultured man accompanied by a shifty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite and affectedly well-mannered people are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Incriminate member in unusual italic note

indicators.note: in places the member inside the other letters
unusual means the letters are made unusual, rearranged

parts.note: E is a musical note
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Accusing a politician over an odd note written in slanted type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the slanted-type word into ILICAT; the member of Parliament goes 'in' after its first letter. 'member' tempts as a limb or arm, but it is the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To involve someone in a crime is to show them to be connected with it.

clue.text: Ruler takes a wife

parts.note: a sultan is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch marries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the pieces; the answer is also a raisin, but here the wife of the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The consort of a Muslim sovereign bears the feminine form of his title.

clue.text: Elementary form is nothing to budding poet

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: budding means the word poet develops into a new form

explanation.surface: An early writer is told that something is worthless to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'budding' makes TOPE from POET; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms of one chemical element with differing numbers of neutrons are variants of that element.

clue.text: Keep a watch on this chap

definitions.text: Keep a watch on this chap

parts.words: Keep a watch on this chap
parts.note: a watch chain bears a man's first name, after Prince ..., so the chap's name is also what keeps a pocket watch secure

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep surveillance on a particular man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep a watch on' reads as spying; in fact the chain is what keeps the watch, fastened to a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain attaching a pocket watch to a waistcoat is named after Queen Victoria's consort, also a man's name.

clue.text: Creator, or Adam, for example

explanation.surface: A maker, perhaps the first man in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam suggests the first man; it is Robert Adam, the 18th-century Scottish designer of buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer of buildings is their creator, and Robert Adam was a famous Georgian designer.

clue.text: Attract to take part in Macbeth

explanation.surface: To draw someone into acting in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the answer is BE WITCH, a role in Macbeth with its three weird sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm or enchant someone is to attract them, and Macbeth's witches are famous parts.

clue.text: Substitute for comfort

explanation.surface: A stand-in for consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: To replace someone on duty and to ease pain are the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking over a shift from a worker, and easing distress, are both senses of the verb.

clue.text: Code of a non-police formation

indicators.note: formation means the letters are formed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, minus the hyphen

explanation.surface: Rules belonging to a group that is not a police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' signals an anagram of A NONPOLICE. 'Code of' points to the French civil code compiled under Bonaparte, whose name the answer's adjective carries.
explanation.definitionFit: The French civil law code of 1804 is named after the emperor Bonaparte, so the adjective completes that title.

clue.text: It may raise an old question of decline

definitions.text: It may raise an old question

explanation.surface: Something prompting a dated query about falling off.
explanation.walkthrough: As an archaic verb form, this word starts questions like 'Wilt thou?' in old English; as a modern verb it means to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic second-person form of 'will' opens old-fashioned questions, and flowers droop and fade when they decline.

clue.text: Flower-girl in play idle vocally

parts.note: the flower-seller in Shaw's Pygmalion; her surname, spoken, sounds like doing little, which is being idle

explanation.surface: A girl selling flowers in a stage show, lazily speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine of Shaw's Pygmalion sells flowers in Covent Garden; her surname said out loud sounds like 'do little', a lazy, idle way to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's Pygmalion centres on a Cockney flower seller taught to speak like a lady by Professor Higgins.

clue.text: Loss of energy?

parts.note: reads as tiredness, but means a power or gas supply escaping, a physical loss of energy from pipes or wires

explanation.surface: A question about someone feeling drained.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cryptic sense: not fatigue but gas or electricity escaping from a system.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape of gas, fluid or current through a hole or fault is such an escape of supply.

clue.text: Union lobby Council Chamber

parts.note: a guild is a union of craftsmen
a hall is a lobby or entrance area

explanation.surface: A trade union's lobbying of a council meeting room.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's council meets in its medieval building of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The hall of a town's guild became the seat of its corporation, its town hall.

clue.text: Curse instructive for Katherina

explanation.surface: A word of damnation that teaches a lesson to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Katherina is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew; split, the answer is an instruction to her, BE SHREW. As one word it is an archaic curse ('Beshrew me').
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb means to wish evil upon, as in Shakespeare's 'beshrew me', and split it tells Katherina what to be.

clue.text: Tape of Liszt heard in entrance to 12

parts.note: Liszt said out loud sounds like list, and a list is a record
the first letter of the answer to 12 down, the council chamber

explanation.surface: A tape of the composer Liszt played in a hall's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Liszt said out loud sounds like 'list', another word for a record. 'in' is taken as written, and the entrance to 12 is the G of GUILDHALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An audio or video tape holds sounds or images captured for playback.

clue.text: Glove maker serves the family

parts.note: serves means does, as in 'that will do'
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A craftsman making gloves who works for his relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glove maker' is not a person but the soft leather gloves are made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft leather from a deer or lamb skin is a material used for fine gloves.

clue.text: Watch old bowler initially deliver ball

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of bowler

parts.note: to serve is to deliver the ball in tennis

explanation.surface: A veteran cricket bowler watching himself start an over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket but only its first letter is used; serving is the tennis delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch is to observe or look at attentively.

clue.text: Could be useable as a main colour

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form another word if rearranged

explanation.surface: A colour that might be usable as a principal one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the old poetic word for the sea, not 'principal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the ocean, so its colour is the shade of the sea.

clue.text: Case for a specialist at the Embassy

explanation.surface: A legal case concerning an expert at a foreign mission.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a slim briefcase; the other a diplomatic staff member with a specialist area, such as a military or press attaché.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim document briefcase shares its name with an embassy official assigned to a particular field.

clue.text: Country of grassland or range

indicators.note: of means the country is drawn out of the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A nation made up of grassland and mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans grassLAND OR RAnge.
explanation.definitionFit: A small principality in the Pyrenees is a sovereign country.

clue.text: Bird almost electric when shifting

indicators.note: shifting means the remaining letters shift into a new order
almost means the word electric is cut short of its last letter

explanation.surface: A bird nearly electrocuted as it moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last C of ELECTRIC, giving ELECTRI; 'when shifting' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In falconry the male hawk, especially the peregrine, is a third smaller than the female.

clue.text: Serious listener has a secluded retreat

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
a nest is a cosy secluded retreat

explanation.surface: A grave person with a hideaway to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere and solemn people are grave and serious in manner.

clue.text: Group leader is a model servant

parts.note: a model is a standard to measure by
a bearer is a servant or porter, as in colonial India

explanation.surface: A head of a group is an ideal domestic helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The person carrying a flag at the head of a march or army leads the group, and figuratively heads a movement.

clue.text: By word of mouth the castle lacks comfort

indicators.note: lacks means the castle's name goes without the comforting word

parts.note: Balmoral is the royal family's castle in Scotland
balm is a soothing comfort

explanation.surface: A spoken report says the castle has no comforts.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL, the royal castle in Aberdeenshire, 'lacks' BALM, leaving the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written communication is passed on by speech, as with oral tradition.

clue.text: Pretty well describes the force of gravity

definitions.text: well describes the force of gravity

explanation.surface: Something quite apt for describing gravitational pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty well' looks like 'fairly well' but splits: 'Pretty' is one definition, and the rest is gravity's pulling nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-looking people are appealing, and gravity is a force pulling bodies towards each other.

clue.text: Bring to light by working a lever

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Uncovering something by operating a lever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by working' rearranges A LEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose or uncover something is to expose it to view.

clue.text: Jet needs volatile fuel initially

indicators.note: initially says the fuel word goes at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: gas is a fuel
volatile in the sense of fickle and flighty, light-headed

explanation.surface: An aircraft requires an explosive fuel to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' suggests an aircraft; here it is a gas jet, a lamp burning a flame. 'initially' puts GAS first.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas jet is a burner giving a flame for illumination, the Victorian street lamp.
